sun.upright:
Aries and Libra sit opposite each other on the wheel, so this is the one card in the deck that comes at an Aries Sun from directly across the table. You're cardinal fire, ruled by Mars. You decide in a second, you're usually right, and you'd sooner fix a mistake later than stand around discussing it first. Justice is the other end of that same axis. It wants the case heard before anything is decided, and it wants both sides heard, including the one you'd normally talk over. The saving grace is that Air and Fire get on. The card feeds your fire instead of damping it, so the pause it asks for costs you less than you'd expect.

What it feels like from the inside is being asked to show your working. The Emperor is Aries's own Major, and he rules by decree, which suits you fine. Justice rules by evidence. I've seen plenty of Aries Suns get prickly with this card because it feels like being slowed down on purpose, and waiting has always felt to you like losing ground. It doesn't cost you ground here. A decision you've actually checked holds up when someone pokes at it, and you'll be glad of that in a fortnight when somebody does.

At work it's the call you'd normally make in ten seconds that deserves an afternoon and a second opinion. At home it's the argument where you were seventy per cent right and spent the whole time defending the other thirty as well. Next time that happens, say which bit you got wrong before anyone has to point it out.
sun.reversed:
Upside down, Justice lets an Aries Sun decide that the fair answer is whichever one you'd already picked. You skip the listening because it bores you, you back yourself hard, and the other side never really gets a hearing. From the inside it feels like clarity. To everyone else it looks as though you announced the result and then held the vote. Mars rules Aries and hates waiting, and here it won't wait for anything, least of all the facts.

The other version is quieter and hotter. Something unfair was done to you, a small thing, and you've been chewing on it for weeks, rehearsing what you'll say. It shows at work in a decision you pushed through a meeting, and at home in a row where the verdict was in before the other person opened their mouth. Leave the next big call for a day. Ask the person you're sure is wrong to explain it once more, and listen to the whole answer.

moon.upright:
An Aries Moon feels things fast and gets them out fast. Something annoys you, you say so, and ten minutes later you've forgotten it, though the person you said it to often hasn't. Mars rules Aries, so your feelings come out as action, the slammed cupboard, the sharp text, the long hard run. Justice sits at the far end of the wheel from your Moon, and what it asks your feelings to do is wait long enough to be checked. Air and Fire are friendly elements, so the card doesn't put your fire out. It just gives it somewhere to go.

What you'll notice is a gap opening between feeling a thing and acting on it, and the gap will itch. Your Moon treats a feeling as a fact. The card keeps asking whose side you haven't heard yet, whether the person you're furious with had a reason, whether the anger's about them or about the day you've had. To be honest, a lot of the time the anger's justified. Knowing exactly who it's for and how much of it they've earned tends to make it land better, and it clears faster too.

It shows most with a partner, who often gets the full blast of something that started at work, and with a friend you cut off mid-sentence because you'd already decided how the story ended. In the body it's heat with nowhere to go, a tight chest, bad sleep after a row. When the surge comes, say what you need out loud before you aim it at anyone, and give them room to answer.
moon.reversed:
With Justice reversed, an Aries Moon lets the heat win and the checking never happens. You react at full tilt and decide afterwards that you were only being fair. The other form is the tally, every time you felt hard done by, filed away and brought out in the next fight. Usually your temper blows over in an hour. This time it sets.

It bites close to home, with the people who get a verdict you reached in the first two seconds, and in a grudge you keep feeding because dropping it feels like admitting you were wrong. Sleep goes ragged while a slight is circling. Mars rules this Moon and wants to hit back. Give the feeling one full day with no action at all, and see whether it still looks like an injustice in the morning.

rising.upright:
Aries rising comes through the door already moving. Mars rules your chart, and strangers tend to read you as quick, direct, a bit of a challenge, the one who'll speak first and decide first. With Aries on the Ascendant, Libra sits on your Descendant, the cusp of the seventh house, which is the sign of the people who come toward you from the other side. So Justice isn't foreign to your chart at all. It's the part of it you usually meet in other people, and this draw asks you to wear some of it yourself. Air and Fire are friendly, so it won't blunt you. It gives the speed something to steer by.

Your instinct is to size up a room in a heartbeat and act on it. The card wants the verdict held open a little longer. People already see decisiveness in you, and what's on offer is for them to see fairness too, a sense that the first thing you do somewhere new is take everyone's measure and only then stake a claim. For Aries rising that's genuinely hard, because the pause feels like weakness. It usually reads to other people as confidence, the kind that doesn't need to go first.

It plays out in interviews, where you tend to answer before the question's finished, and in any new group where you've quietly appointed yourself the one who decides. It shows when someone challenges you early and you have a choice between flattening them and hearing them out. Walk into the next unfamiliar room and say less than you want to for the first ten minutes, and notice what you pick up.
rising.reversed:
Turned the other way, Justice can make Aries rising treat every first meeting as a contest. You come in reading the room for who to beat, call it being sharp, and the fair-minded version of you never gets through the door. Or you overcorrect into a stiff, careful politeness that isn't you at all, and people can tell it's a front.

It shows in the handshake with a bit too much grip, and in a meeting where your first move is to establish who's senior. It shows when a stranger asks a reasonable question and you hear it as an attack. With Libra on your seventh, the people opposite you often hold the fairness you're missing, and you can end up fighting them for it. Let the other person set some of the pace in the next first conversation, and see whether you lose anything by it.

sun.upright:
Venus rules Taurus, and Venus rules Libra, the sign this card belongs to. So underneath it all a Taurus Sun and Justice want the same thing, which is for things to be worth what they're said to be worth. The difference is where the worth lives. Your Venus is in fixed earth, and you measure value by what you can hold, count and rely on for years. The card's Venus is in air, and it measures value by whether the exchange was fair. Earth and Air are opposed elements, and Taurus and Libra sit five signs apart, a quincunx, which in practice means the two keep needing small adjustments to get along at all.

The friction you'll feel is between proof and principle. Justice keeps pushing you toward the fair thing when the fair thing costs you something solid, and your instinct is to trust what's concrete over what's merely argued. Taurus Suns dig in when they're asked to reopen something settled, and this card is asking exactly that, probably about a figure or an arrangement you stopped questioning a while ago. The Hierophant is your sign's Major, the card of how things have always been done, and he's on your side of the argument here, which is part of why it's hard.

It lands on money and on what you think you're owed, the pay rise you've decided is yours, the split with a sibling over what a parent left. It lands on a friendship where you've been quietly keeping score in favours. Put your reasoning on the table, ask for theirs, and let the fair number move you even if it comes in under the comfortable one.
sun.reversed:
A Taurus Sun can use its trust in the concrete to duck a fair reckoning, insisting the only real measure is the one that happens to suit you. What's mine is mine and the matter's closed. The Venus you share with this card curls inward, keeping where it ought to be trading, and the principle of the thing never gets looked at because looking might cost you some comfort.

It surfaces around money and in slow grudges, the debt you're owed and won't let go of, the share you're quietly holding back because handing it over pinches. Fixed earth is slow to move and slower to admit it's been wrong, so this can harden into a settled story about how you were only being sensible. Ask yourself the plain question you've been avoiding, which is whether the fair split and the comfortable split are the same split, and act on the answer if they aren't.

moon.upright:
A Taurus Moon settles when the ground holds still. The same routine, the same people, a fed and rested body, a house that smells like home. Justice asks something your Moon finds a bit strange, which is to check a feeling for fairness before you let it run the household. Venus rules both Taurus and Libra, so the wish underneath is one you'd recognise, since you both want peace. Yours is built out of comfort and the card's is built out of balance, and with the two signs five apart and Earth set against Air, getting from one to the other takes some fiddling.

The rub is that Air wants to talk a feeling through and your Earth just wants it soothed. When something's unfair to you, your body knows before your head does, a heaviness, a loss of appetite or the reverse, and your first move is toward whatever feels nice. It works for an evening. What the card is pointing at is the imbalance that keeps making you need the soothing, and that's usually something you've carried so long you've stopped noticing the weight.

It shows up in the shared load at home, the chores and bills and emotional upkeep you've been absorbing so as not to disturb the calm. It shows in the fridge and the bank account on a bad week. Name the imbalance once, plainly, to the person it involves, and let the conversation be uncomfortable until it's actually sorted.
moon.reversed:
Off true, a Taurus Moon turns comfort into a wall. A hurt that ought to be looked at gets buried under routine, food, spending, the familiar, and you call the numbness peace. The imbalance doesn't go anywhere. Fixed signs keep what they're given, so it sinks into the body and the mood and stays there for months.

You'll find it in the resentment you won't name because naming it would rock the house, and in the share of a load you keep carrying while telling yourself you don't mind. You'll find it in comfort habits that get a little heavier each week something is off. Venus rules this Moon, and Venus likes ease far too much to start an argument. Start one anyway, gently. Say the unfair thing to the person it involves, and sit through the wobble without reaching for the biscuit tin.

rising.upright:
Taurus rising arrives calm. Venus rules your chart, and strangers usually meet someone unhurried, pleasant, comfortable in their own skin, in no rush to prove anything. Justice belongs to Libra, the other sign Venus rules, so this is your chart ruler turning up in its airier clothes. The two signs sit five apart and Earth and Air don't naturally agree, so the fit takes some work. Counting whole signs from a Taurus Ascendant, Libra lands on your sixth house, the house of the working day, and that's often where this card shows itself first.

What people meet in you is reliability. Justice asks them to meet fairness as well, to feel that your calm comes with a real willingness to hear their side. The trouble for Taurus rising is that calm can read as immovable. You take your time forming a view, and once it's formed you're slow to reopen it. That's usually a strength. With this card drawn, though, somebody new is going to ask you to look again at a thing you'd settled, and the way you handle being asked is most of what they'll remember about you.

You'll see it at work, when a colleague assumes you're easygoing and finds a firm line underneath, and when a new client wants a quick decision and gets a considered one. It shows in how you treat a newcomer who does things differently from you. Let your first response to someone new be an actual question about how they see it, and once in a while let them watch you change your mind.
rising.reversed:
Taurus rising with this card upside down can look reasonable and be completely immovable. The face stays pleasant, the voice stays even, and underneath the view is set and nothing anyone says will shift it. People take a while to work out that the openness was a courtesy, and they don't love it when they do.

It shows when someone new suggests a change at work and you go warm and unbudging at the same time, and in a reputation for being lovely and impossible to negotiate with. It shows when stubbornness gets called having standards. Venus rules your chart and it's good at keeping the surface nice. Catch the moment your face stays friendly after your mind has shut, and say the doubt out loud, so the other person at least knows where they stand.

sun.upright:
Gemini and Libra are both air signs, four apart, a trine, so a Gemini Sun and Justice speak the same language from the first word. Seeing every side of a question, arguing it out, reasoning your way toward what's fair, that's already how your mind runs. Mercury rules Gemini and it's quick, curious and very good at making a case. The card isn't asking you to become anything new. It hands you a sharper version of something you already carry and asks you to use it properly.

The catch, and it's the usual one when a card shares your element, is that it turns everything up, the too-much included. A Gemini Sun can see all sides so clearly that it can argue any of them, and fairness slides into never landing anywhere. Or cleverness takes over and you win the point without settling the truth. Look at what's in the figure's right hand. It's a sword, held straight up, and it's there for cutting. The Lovers is Gemini's own Major, and that card is about a choice too, so between the two of them you keep getting walked back to the moment where you have to pick.

You'll feel it at work in negotiating, writing, pitching, anywhere your quickness shows, where the danger is arguing a fair case so well you forget to check it's the true one. You'll feel it with friends when you play devil's advocate one round too long and somebody gets hurt. Pick the point where you stop turning it over, commit to the fair answer, and let the cleverer angle go unused.
sun.reversed:
Off kilter, a Gemini Sun uses all that verbal skill to talk itself out of a fair conclusion, or to win a case it half knows is crooked. You can make almost anything sound reasonable, and reversed that's the whole problem, because the cleverest account in the room isn't always the honest one and you're good enough to blur the difference. Keeping the question permanently open means never having to stand behind an answer.

It shows in slippery agreements, the promise worded so there's a way out later, the argument you won on points while knowing you were wrong. It can also look like restless second-guessing that you call being open-minded. Mercury rules Gemini and loves a clever answer. Write down the plain, unclever version of what happened, the one a child could follow, and hold yourself to that one.

moon.upright:
Gemini Moons sort out a feeling by talking about it. A long phone call, a voice note, a group chat at midnight, and by the end you know what you felt, which you didn't at the start. Mercury rules Gemini, so understanding comes before comfort for you. Justice sits a trine away in the same element, and its habit of checking whether something was fair fits your emotional wiring as if it were made for it. When someone upsets you, your first instinct is already to work out whether they were being unfair, or whether you were.

Same element means amplified, though, and a Gemini Moon can think about a feeling so thoroughly that it never actually gets felt. You look at the hurt from six angles and build a generous case for everyone involved, the person who caused it included, and somewhere in all that reasoning the raw thing gets explained away. You end up being fair to everyone except yourself, and a bit puzzled about why you still feel flat.

It comes up with the people closest to you, where you explain your feelings so well and so quickly that they arrive as arguments. It shows at night, going back over a conversation and rewording what you should have said. Let one feeling stay just a feeling for a whole evening, and tell someone the unreasoned version of it, even if it comes out clumsy.
moon.reversed:
Gemini Moons can talk a feeling to death when Justice turns over. You go over a hurt again and again until it's a debate with no floor, or you get so good at seeing the other person's side that your own never gets a turn, and you call that fairness. The talking that usually settles you only spins.

It surfaces as sleep lost to a conversation you keep replaying with fresh lines, and as telling three friends three slightly different versions and believing each one as you say it. It shows when being reasonable is a way of avoiding saying you're hurt. Mercury wants to understand before it feels anything. Give it the night off. Say the plain feeling in five words or fewer, and if you have to judge anyone, judge whether you've been fair to yourself.

rising.upright:
Gemini rising meets people mid-sentence, quick, curious, changing register to suit whoever's in front of you. Strangers usually find you clever and easy company, if a little hard to pin down. Justice suits your manner well. It's the same element, a trine away, so the even-handedness it brings sharpens your style. The both-sides quality is already in how you talk to someone new, and people who've only just met you often come away thinking you'd be a good person to have on a jury.

Where it gets pointed is that Gemini rising can be so adaptable that people aren't sure which version of you is the real one. Fair-mindedness is easy for you to perform. Holding a position steady when a quick, winning line is right there is the harder part, and it's what the card is actually after. I've watched Gemini risings talk their way into and out of the same opinion inside one dinner, charmingly, and leave the whole table unsure what they think.

You'll see it at parties and interviews, where you charm people and leave them unsure they could rely on you, and in how you handle an early disagreement with someone who doesn't know you yet. The next time you take a position in a new room, make it one you'd still hold tomorrow, and let a stranger watch you commit to it.
rising.reversed:
Upside down, Justice can turn Gemini rising's fairness into a performance with nobody behind it. You show every newcomer the reasonable, sees-all-sides face while keeping your actual view tucked away, or you flit between positions so fast that no one, you included, can say what you stand for. The clever manner wins the room and nothing honest gets said.

It shows in a first impression that's charming and slightly untrustworthy at once, and in arguing a stranger's side and your own inside the same conversation. It shows when you use a joke to slide past a straight question. On a date it can look like agreeing with everything and being forgotten by the weekend. Mercury rules your chart and it's quick on its feet. Slow it down. Give one plain answer about where you stand, and let someone new meet the version of you that stays put.

sun.upright:
Cancer Suns build a life around the people they keep safe. You're cardinal water, ruled by the Moon, protective and loyal, with a long memory for who was there for you and who wasn't. Justice comes at that from a hard angle. Libra is square to Cancer, three signs off, the two sharing only the cardinal urge to get things moving. Air and Water are neutral in this system, neither friends nor enemies, so they have to be introduced, and the introduction here is a bit stiff. You decide by how something feels and whether it protects your own. The card wants it decided by what's fair to everyone, people outside your circle included.

A square is friction that forces a decision, and the one this forces is between loyalty and fairness. That can be genuinely painful for a Cancer Sun. Putting your own family or your own team on the same scale as a stranger feels close to betrayal, and your instinct is to close ranks. The Chariot is Cancer's Major, and its driver goes forward inside a hard shell. Justice asks you to lower the shell for a moment and look at your own side the way an outsider would.

It lands in family, in the dispute where the fair answer doesn't protect your side, and with the parent or sibling you've defended long past the point of honesty. It lands at work, when backing your team means overlooking what they actually got wrong. Take one of these and imagine the people in it were strangers to you, and see what the fair answer looks like from there.
sun.reversed:
Loyalty takes over from fairness when a Cancer Sun draws this card reversed. Whatever protects your own becomes your definition of fair, and anyone outside the circle gets a harsher measure, though you'd rarely admit there are two. The square that should push you toward an honest decision sets into a defensive crouch instead, and feeling decides what the facts are.

It shows in family loyalty that shades into covering for someone, in holding a grudge on behalf of a person you love long after they've moved on, in hearing any criticism of your people as an attack on you. The Moon rules Cancer, and when it feels threatened it goes into its shell and pulls everyone it loves in after it. Notice when you're guarding your own instead of looking, and ask whether you'd call it fair if a stranger's family did exactly the same thing to yours.

moon.upright:
The Moon rules Cancer, so a Cancer Moon is the Moon at home, feeling everything at full depth and remembering all of it. Every kindness, every slight, the exact tone of a phone call years ago. Justice stands square to that, three signs away, and its cool Air and your deep Water don't blend on their own. The card is asking your feelings to be checked for fairness, and to a Cancer Moon that can feel almost cold, like being told a very real hurt has to prove its case before it's allowed.

The friction is real and it's there to move you. Your feelings arrive complete and certain, and this card keeps asking whether the story your mood tells is the fair one, whether the person who hurt you meant it the way you've filed it. Sometimes they did. Sometimes the memory has been doing the filing for twenty years and got a few things wrong. That's a hard thing to look at, because the hurt was real either way.

It shows around home and family, with the people who can flood you fastest, and in a slight you've nursed for years that may have started as a misunderstanding. It shows in how an old wound colours the way you read a new one. In the body it can feel like being waterlogged while something sits unresolved. When the next wave comes, let it crest and pass before you act, then take the memory out again once you're calm and see if it still reads the same.
moon.reversed:
Reversed, the card lets a Cancer Moon's tides write the verdict and never go back to check it. A hurt from years ago is treated as settled fact, and anyone who questions the story joins the list of people who wounded you. The mood has already ruled, so nothing gets looked at again.

It shows in grudges that outlive their cause, in old betrayals read into new and ordinary situations, in retreating into the shell and calling it self-protection. A parent or a sibling is often at the centre of it, even when the person in front of you is someone else entirely. Sleep and appetite swing with whatever's unresolved. Take one old, certain hurt and genuinely reopen it. Ask what someone who loved everyone involved would have seen if they'd been in the room, and let their answer count for something.

rising.upright:
Cancer rising comes into a room carefully. You feel out whether it's safe before you commit, and strangers tend to read you as gentle, kind, a little guarded, quick to look after whoever seems to need it. The Moon rules your chart, so your face shows the weather. Justice sits square to your Ascendant, a cardinal cousin three signs off, and its cool Air doesn't sit naturally with your watery way in. Counting whole signs, Libra falls on your fourth house, so the card has a strong link to home and family for you, and a lot of what you know about fairness you learned at the kitchen table.

Your first read on someone is emotional and protective. You can be wary of a person who's done nothing wrong, or soft on someone who charmed the tender part of you, and the card wants a beat of level assessment folded in before you sort people into in and out. That's a real adjustment for Cancer rising. The protective instinct is usually right. It's also usually quicker than the facts.

People you've just met feel looked after, and they also sense they've been quietly filed under safe or not safe. It shows most in how you handle someone new who rubs you the wrong way for no reason you can name. Give that person a proper hearing before the feeling files them, and notice how often your guard was protecting you from nothing at all.
rising.reversed:
The guard does all the judging when Justice turns over on Cancer rising. You decide in seconds whether a new person is safe, and that snap feeling becomes a verdict you won't reopen. Or the careful front turns moody, a coolness strangers can't account for because whatever's going on is happening where they can't see it.

It shows in first impressions that run hot or cold for no visible reason, and in pulling back the moment someone feels unsafe and calling it instinct. It shows when a newcomer pays for an old hurt they had nothing to do with, often because they look or sound like someone from home. The Moon rules your chart and it remembers. Let your first feeling about a stranger stay a question for a week, and give the level part of you a say before the shell closes.

sun.upright:
Leo Suns want to be seen doing something that matters, and they like to be generous while they're at it. You're fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, warm, loyal and very good at being the middle of the room. Justice gets on with that better than you might think. Libra sits two signs from Leo, a sextile, a friendly opening between the two, and the card's Air feeds your Fire. The thing about a sextile is that it only helps if you use it. The fairness on offer here is something you pick up on purpose, and nobody's going to hand it to you.

What it asks of your pride is that some of the light goes to other people. You're generous by nature, and generosity and fairness aren't quite the same thing. You can give lavishly and still need the credit for it, the round you bought, the favour you did, the idea that was mostly yours. Strength is Leo's own Major, and it shows a kind of power that doesn't have to announce itself. Justice sits close to that. It asks whether the credit landed where it belongs, and it doesn't mind at all if some of it belongs to someone else.

It shows at work when a win was really the team's and your name went on it, and in a friendship where you're used to being the one everyone gathers around and somebody quietly needs a turn. Being told you were wrong in front of people is the other test. The next time you're praised for something shared, say out loud who else did it, by name.
sun.reversed:
Knocked out of true, a Leo Sun tilts the credit its own way and calls it earned. The story of any success has you at the centre, and everyone else's share quietly shrinks, because some of the warmth you give out was always partly a bid for applause. The Sun rules Leo, and when it's hurt it needs to be seen even more.

It shows when praise gets hoarded, when a fair complaint about you gets treated as an insult, when you're wounded that a friend needed the attention for once. Pride does the accounting, and pride tends to find in your favour. It can show with children too, a parent who needs a child's achievements to reflect well on them. Give away one piece of credit you'd normally keep, and put up with how exposed that feels without going looking for the next compliment.

moon.upright:
A Leo Moon needs to feel adored. Nothing shallow about it, you just need your warmth to be noticed and met, and when the love in the room isn't coming back your way you go either very cold or very dramatic. Fixed fire, ruled by the Sun, you give a lot. Justice offers a friendly hand here, sitting a sextile off and feeding your Fire with its Air, though like any sextile it only helps if you take it. What it gives you is a clearer way of telling whether you're genuinely being taken for granted or just hungry for reassurance.

What tugs is that your heart keeps a warm, generous tally and expects the same warmth back, and the card asks you to look at that tally honestly. Sometimes the appreciation is there and your need for it is simply loud. Sometimes you really are giving far more than you get, and the card wants that said plainly, which is harder for a Leo Moon than sulking. Strength is your sign's Major, and there's a quiet courage in just saying 'I need more from you' without any of the performance around it.

It shows with the people whose attention matters most, the partner whose praise you fish for, the friend you give and give to while privately counting. The body registers it as a kind of deflation after a night where nobody noticed. When you feel unseen, check whether it's fair before you act hurt, and then ask for the thing you actually want.
moon.reversed:
Out of true, a Leo Moon's need for love turns into a scale that only ever reads in its own favour. You feel unappreciated on a hair trigger, keep count of every time you gave and weren't thanked, and go icy or theatrical to pull the attention back. Whether you've offered the same warmth you're asking for never comes up.

It shows in a sulk that punishes someone for not noticing you, in generosity that comes with an invisible bill, in needing to be the wronged party in every story. The Sun rules Leo and needs to be warm to feel alive, and here the warmth has turned into a transaction. Next time you feel slighted, before the performance starts, ask yourself whether the other person actually owed you what you're missing, and say what you need in one plain sentence.

rising.upright:
Leo rising makes an entrance whether it means to or not. The Sun rules your chart, and people meeting you usually notice the warmth and the confidence first, a bit of theatre in the way you fill a doorway. Justice gets along with that nicely. It's a sextile away and airy where you're fiery, so it lifts the charisma. What it adds is an even-handedness people can feel under the warmth, though as with any sextile you have to pick the opening up yourself. Leo rising already has a natural authority, and with this card it reads as the authority of someone who'll hear both sides.

The thing to watch is that a big, warm first impression can quietly make everything about you. You're genuinely generous with your attention, but the spotlight does follow you into rooms and leave other people in the shade. Justice wants the entrance to be fair as well as bright. To be honest, the Leo risings who get this right are some of the most magnetic people I know, because whatever attention they draw, they hand a good share of it round.

It shows in first meetings where you charm the room and realise on the drive home you learned nothing about anyone in it, and in how you handle a stranger who isn't impressed. Walk into the next new situation and put the light on someone else early. Ask them a real question and stay with the answer.
rising.reversed:
Leo rising with Justice upside down can turn the whole entrance into a request for applause. You come in warm and magnetic, but it's all pointed at being admired, and people leave feeling performed at. Or, stung once, the confident manner goes cold, and you punish a room for not giving you enough.

First impressions dazzle and then sour when the attention moves on, and a stranger's indifference gets taken as a personal slight. It shows in conversations where you're the only one who gets to finish a story, and at work in needing to be the one who presents, every single time. The Sun rules your chart and it likes to be the centre, which is fine until it can't share. Catch the moment your warmth is fishing for a reaction, and try meeting one new person with plain interest and no need for them to be impressed.

sun.upright:
Virgo Suns take pride in getting it right. Mutable earth, ruled by Mercury, you notice the typo on page forty and the gap in the plan, and being useful is a point of pride. Libra is the sign right next door, and neighbouring signs have surprisingly little in common. The card's Air rubs against your Earth, the old argument between the idea of a thing and the plain fact of it. Each of you has what the other lacks. You bring the exactness Libra tends to float above, and Justice brings a sense of the whole situation that close work can lose.

The friction is that your version of fairness is usually accuracy, the facts right, the standard met, the numbers adding up. The card keeps widening that out to whether the outcome is actually fair to the people in it. You can be scrupulously correct and still miss the just thing, and I've seen Virgo Suns do exactly that and be baffled when someone's upset, because every detail they raised was true. The Hermit is Virgo's Major, a card of doing the careful work alone. Justice pulls you out of the back room and asks you to consider the person as well as the paperwork.

It shows at work where you hold a high standard and tip into picking the one fault in someone's good effort, and in a friendship where you keep a precise mental record of who did what. It shows most in how hard you are on your own small failings. Before you correct the detail, say one fair thing about the whole, and let some things be good enough.
sun.reversed:
A Virgo Sun reversed turns fairness into fault-finding. The careful record becomes a way to hold everyone, yourself included, to a standard that always finds something short, and you call that being fair when it's closer to being hard. The details win and the wider justice of the situation gets lost underneath them.

It shows in criticism that lands as the last word on someone's genuine effort, in a grudge kept in exact detail long after it stopped mattering, in the private harshness you turn on your own mistakes. Mercury rules Virgo and it's excellent at spotting what's wrong, and here it won't switch off. Worry can settle in the gut when the standard never lets up. Ease off for a moment and ask the wider question, whether the person in front of you is being treated fairly or just being measured.

moon.upright:
Order is what calms a Virgo Moon. The bench wiped down, the list ticked off, the problem fixed. Mercury rules Virgo, so feelings often come out as tasks for you, and when someone you love is struggling your first move is to help in some practical way. Justice sits one sign over, a neighbour speaking a different language, its Air not quite meeting your Earth. Checking a feeling for fairness doesn't come as naturally to you as sorting it out does, and you and this card have different instincts about what makes a thing right.

The awkward part is that your care tends to arrive as correction, and the card asks whether that's fair to the person receiving it. More often it asks whether you're being fair to yourself. A Virgo Moon runs a harsh inner audit. You'll forgive a friend for missing a deadline in about four seconds and still be annoyed with yourself about something from last year, and the card sees the double standard even if you don't.

It shows with family and close friends, where love comes out as noticing what they could do better, and in the way one unfinished job can nag at you all evening. In the body it's tension that builds when things feel out of order, usually in the stomach or the shoulders. When the urge to fix or criticise comes up, ask whether you'd forgive a friend for falling short of that standard, and give yourself the same answer.
moon.reversed:
Turned over, Justice leaves a Virgo Moon with a scale that never balances. Nothing is ever quite right, the audit runs day and night, and you punish yourself hardest of all, calling it having standards. The fairness the card is asking for gets buried under a to-do list that stands in for feeling safe.

It shows in criticism that leaks onto the people you love, in anxiety that spikes when something can't be fixed, in the quiet belief that you haven't earned rest until everything's done. At work it can look like staying late to redo something that was already fine. The body carries it as a clenched, wound-up tiredness, and sleep goes light. Put the list down for one evening on purpose, leave something undone where you can see it, and notice that nothing terrible happens.

rising.upright:
Virgo rising walks into a new situation noticing everything. What needs doing, what's out of place, who's struggling. Strangers tend to read you as modest, competent, a touch reserved until you've taken the measure of things. Mercury rules your chart. Justice sits right next door to your Ascendant, close but speaking a different tongue, and its Air against your Earth sets up a small friction between sorting a thing and being fair about it. Counting whole signs, Libra falls on your second house, which often means fairness turns up for you as a question about money, what you charge, what you accept, what you think you're worth.

What rubs is that your first instinct with people is to assess and quietly correct. The card asks you to hold the appraisal back long enough to see the person evenly. You can come across as helpful and faintly critical at once, and strangers feel measured before they feel met. Some Virgo risings I've known had no idea they did this until somebody told them, years in.

You'll catch it in a first meeting where you've clocked what someone's doing wrong before you've caught their name, and in how you handle a newcomer who's messy or vague in a way that grates. It shows when you're quoting a price and knock something off before anyone's asked. Say one thing you genuinely rate about a new person before any of the rest, and quote your full rate.
rising.reversed:
Virgo rising reversed makes the observant manner a critical one. You meet new people already tallying their faults, come across as helpful while quietly judging, and strangers feel inspected. Or you go so self-conscious about your own flaws that you pull back and read as cold and hard to reach.

It shows in a first impression where your competence comes with a faint air of disapproval, and in correcting a newcomer over something small and losing them for good. It shows when nerves make you pick holes to feel in control. Mercury rules your chart and it's a detail planet, and detail is a poor way to meet someone. Meet the next new person with one honest note of what's good before anything you'd fix, and leave the fixing for another day.

sun.upright:
This is your own card. Justice is Libra's Major, so drawing it for a Libra Sun is the sign meeting its own portrait, and there's no angle to work out or element to translate. It's Air on Air, cardinal air ruled by Venus, your own nature handed straight back to you at full strength. That's lovely, and it's also a lot, because when a card and a sign are this close it shows you the best of you and the too-much of you at the same time.

The best is real. Seeing every side, balancing a room, making sure each person gets their due, that's genuinely who you are, and the card confirms it. The too-much is the Libra trap, and you'll know it well. The weighing that never lands. The fairness to everyone that leaves you last in the queue. The dread of a decision that might upset somebody. Look at the card again. The figure is holding a sword as well as the scales, and the sword is pointing straight up, ready. Being cardinal, you're meant to start things, and choosing is how anything starts.

It shows at work, where you mediate everyone else's disputes and stall on your own call, and in a relationship where keeping the peace has quietly cost you your position on something that matters. It shows in how long a menu can take. Make the next decision the moment you have enough to be fair, and let it stand even though it isn't perfectly balanced.
sun.reversed:
A Libra Sun's gift for fairness folds back on itself when this card reverses. The weighing never stops, so nothing gets decided, or you tip things to keep the peace and call that fair when you've really just ducked the conflict. It being your own card doubles it, and the stall becomes a way of life, every choice put off until someone else makes it for you.

It shows in decisions that go stale because you couldn't bear to disappoint anyone, in agreeing with whoever's in the room, in a resentment that builds because you gave your own side away to keep things smooth. Venus rules Libra and loves things pleasant, and here pleasant is costing you. Make the next small choice quickly and on its merits, and notice that disappointing one person is sometimes simply the fair result.

moon.upright:
A Libra Moon can't settle while something feels unfair or someone in the room is upset. Venus rules Libra, and you need harmony around you the way other people need a decent night's sleep. You reason your way to calm. Justice is your own card, so this is your emotional nature amplified, Air meeting Air, the need for balance turned all the way up. When it's working, you're the one who senses the tension in a room before anyone says a word and quietly sorts it out.

The trouble is that a Libra Moon can be so busy keeping everyone else level that its own feelings never get looked at. You'll swallow an unfairness done to you to keep the peace and then wonder why you feel hollow a week later. The calm you bought was real. You just paid for all of it yourself. I've seen Libra Moons do this for years in a marriage without either person quite noticing.

It shows with a partner or close friend where you smooth every edge and keep your own upset to yourself, and in how a raised voice or a sulk in the next room can wreck your whole day. In the body it's an unease that won't lift while something between you and someone else is unresolved. When you feel the pull to give way, put your own need next to theirs and look at both before you decide.
moon.reversed:
Keeping the peace at any cost is how a Libra Moon tends to live this card reversed, and the quiet gets called fairness. You give way, agree, smooth things over, and the unfairness you swallowed sits in you as a low unease you can't quite put a name to. It's your own card, so the pattern runs deep, often all the way back to a childhood home where someone had to keep things calm.

It shows in a relationship where you've slowly disappeared into what the other person wants, in friendships where you're always the one who bends, in resentment that leaks out sideways because it never got a straight word. Sleep and appetite waver while something stays lopsided. Say the unbalanced thing plainly to the person involved, and let the argument be short and a bit uncomfortable.

rising.upright:
Libra rising meets the world graciously. You read what a situation needs and adjust to it, and strangers tend to find you charming, even-handed, easy to like, and often the best-mannered person there. Venus rules your chart, and Justice is the card of your own rising sign, Air on Air, so the effect is doubled. People trust you quickly to be fair, and mostly you earn it.

Where the doubling gets tricky is that Libra rising can be so tuned to being liked that the fairness turns into agreeableness. You mirror people so well they see themselves in you and assume you agree with them. Sometimes you don't, and haven't said so, and there's a moment later on, a meeting or a dinner, where they find out and feel slightly misled. The card is asking whether the even face you show is a real opinion or a wish to keep everyone happy. Cardinal air is built to get things going, and an early, honest opinion is one of the ways it does that.

At a first meeting you're instantly likeable and leave people unsure what you actually think, and a stranger whose view strikes you as unfair usually gets a polite nod. It shows in a job interview when you agree with everything the panel says. Let someone new hear an actual opinion of yours early, said gently, and trust them to cope with it.
rising.reversed:
Libra rising reversed uses charm as a way of never being pinned down. You please everyone, agree with the last person who spoke, and the fair-minded face hides the fact that you haven't taken a position at all. It's your own card, so this runs smooth and habitual, years of being liked standing in for being known.

It shows in first impressions that are lovely and a bit weightless, in flattering a view you privately think is unjust, in the people who feel let down when your real opinion finally comes out. Venus rules your chart and wants everyone comfortable, and it will trade almost anything for that. Give one honest, mildly unwelcome opinion to someone new, and let them find out you have a spine.

sun.upright:
Scorpio Suns go all the way in or not at all. Fixed water, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, you want the truth under the surface, you keep your own counsel, and you don't hand out trust or forgiveness lightly. Libra sits right beside Scorpio on the wheel, and neighbours like these share almost nothing. Air and Water are neutral elements, so the card's open, talk-it-through fairness and your deep, private water have to be deliberately introduced before they'll cooperate. You care about truth already. The card cares about it in daylight, said out loud, with everyone given a hearing.

The difference matters. Your sense of justice tends to run underground, intense and personal, a private verdict on who's loyal and who let you down. Justice asks you to bring that up into the open, including the chance that your read of someone's motive is off. That's hard for a Scorpio Sun, because your instinct for what's hidden is usually right, and usually is doing a lot of work in that sentence. Death is Scorpio's Major, a card of clean endings, and Mars gives you the nerve to make one. This card wants you sure of the facts before you do.

It shows in how you handle a betrayal, real or suspected, where giving someone a fair hearing can feel like weakness. It shows in shared money, a will or a joint account, where you sense someone's taking more than their share. Before you pass a private sentence on anyone, tell them what you think they did and let them answer it.
sun.reversed:
A Scorpio Sun with this card reversed keeps the scales underground where no one can see them. You judge people in private, decide what their loyalty is worth, and act on it without ever telling them the charge, so they can't defend themselves and you can't be proven wrong. It feels like protecting yourself. To anyone on the receiving end it's a trial they didn't know they were in.

It shows in a grudge nursed in silence and repaid cold, in cutting someone off for something they never got the chance to explain, in a quiet struggle over shared money or secrets. Mars rules Scorpio and it doesn't forget, and suspicion starts passing itself off as proof. Bring one private verdict into the open and let the person respond, and loosen your grip on what you think their motive was.

moon.upright:
A Scorpio Moon feels everything at depth and shows very little of it. You need to know the real truth of a bond before you can rest in it, and once you've been hurt you remember it in your body for years. Justice sits one sign along, a near neighbour that speaks another language, its clear Air not naturally at home in your fixed Water. Bringing a feeling out into the open to be looked at fairly is a genuine reach for you. Your instinct is to bury it and settle the score quietly later, if at all.

Your emotional justice is powerful and private, and this card asks it to come up where it can be seen and answered. When you feel betrayed you know it in your gut, and the card asks whether your gut has taken in the whole story or only the wound. Sometimes it's right. Sometimes it's an old hurt reading a new person. Mars is Scorpio's traditional ruler, and a Mars Moon is always half ready for a fight, which makes the two hard to tell apart from the inside.

It shows with the few people you let all the way in, where a small breach can set off a total, silent reckoning they never hear about. In the body it's a held tightness, the jaw and the gut, and restless nights when trust is in question. When the urge comes to withdraw and settle it privately, take the feeling to the person instead, and let them have their say before you decide anything.
moon.reversed:
Upturned, the card lets a Scorpio Moon turn a private wound into a life sentence. You go over a betrayal alone, deep underwater, and the verdict comes out absolute, with no appeal and no chance for the other person to explain. You can hold it for years without their ever knowing they were tried.

It shows in a bond cut off for good over something that was never discussed, in reading a fresh betrayal into someone who only reminds you of an old one, in a need for control that calls itself self-protection. Intimacy is often where it's sharpest. The body holds it as a clenched, watchful tension, and sleep suffers. Take one buried verdict and say it out loud to the person it concerns, and let what they say back actually change your mind about something.

rising.upright:
Scorpio rising doesn't give much away. You watch, you listen, you work people out while staying unread yourself, and strangers often feel the intensity before they know a single thing about you. Mars rules your chart, with Pluto as its modern co-ruler. Justice stands next door with a very different manner, open, airy, talking it through, a neighbour you have to make an effort to let in. Counting whole signs, Libra is the sign on your twelfth house, the hidden one, and that suits the way fairness tends to work in you, quietly and behind the scenes, where other people rarely see it.

The difficulty is that your instinct is to withhold and watch, and the card wants your first impression to be fair and even a little transparent about how you're reading people. As it is, strangers can feel judged by you before they've been met, as though they've been tried in a court they can't see. Most of the time you haven't decided anything much. They don't know that, though, and you rarely tell them.

It comes through in a first impression where your intensity reads as suspicion, and in the trust a newcomer is trying to earn from you without knowing the rules. Give one stranger an open hearing, and tell them something you like about them early on in the conversation.
rising.reversed:
When Justice is reversed on Scorpio rising, the guarded manner becomes a closed court. You read everyone and reveal nothing, and pass private judgement on new people who never find out they were being assessed. Or the intensity tips into suspicion, and every stranger gets treated as a possible threat.

Strangers come away feeling scanned. You hold back warmth until someone passes a test you never told them about, and you read hidden motives into people that were never there. It can cost you at work, where colleagues decide you don't like them and stop bringing you things. Mars rules your chart and it's always on guard, and here it's calling control discernment. Meet the next new person with a bit more of you on show, and if you do decide against them, let them see why.

sun.upright:
Sagittarius Suns say what they think. Mutable fire, ruled by Jupiter, you want the big picture and the plain truth, and you get restless the moment life narrows down to the fine print. Justice sits a sextile away, two signs off, and its Air feeds your Fire, so the fairness it brings is a help to you. You already love the truth. What the card adds is the patience to check it, to hold the sweeping thing you just said up against the particular facts of the case.

The tension is that Sagittarian honesty can be honest and unfair at the same time. You tell it like it is, but your version of how it is gets painted with a broad brush, and the card keeps asking whether you've heard the other person's side before you deliver the verdict. Jupiter makes everything bigger, including how sure you feel. Temperance is Sagittarius's own Major, a card of getting the mixture right, and that's close to what Justice is after here, the right amount of conviction for the evidence you've actually got. As with any sextile, it's on offer, and you'll have to reach for it.

You'll see it at work, where your vision is right in outline and unfair in the detail to the people who have to carry it out, and in a friendship where a blunt truth landed harder than you meant. It comes up too when someone holds you to a promise you made casually. Before you give anyone your big honest opinion, check two small facts underneath it, and stay long enough to hear what they say back.
sun.reversed:
A Sagittarius Sun can mistake its own opinion for the truth when this card reverses, and then call saying it fairness. You hand out sweeping verdicts, sure you're being refreshingly honest, and skip the part where you check the facts or ask for the other side, because that feels like being tied down. The bluntness starts to land as careless, sometimes cruel.

It surfaces in a strong view aired without checking it, in promises made large and kept loosely, in a righteousness that holds other people to a standard you let yourself off. Jupiter rules Sagittarius and it's generous with everything, certainty included. The restlessness treats being held to account as a cage. Slow down on the next big pronouncement, look up the detail you'd usually wave away, and stay to answer for what you said.

moon.upright:
A Sagittarius Moon needs room to breathe. You feel best on the move, or looking at something bigger than the mess in front of you, and when emotions turn heavy you get twitchy and want out. Jupiter rules Sagittarius, so you cope with optimism and distance, a drive, a plan, a joke. Justice reaches over from a sextile, its Air lifting your Fire, and it offers a fairer way to deal with feelings than heading for the horizon. It's a friendly offer, and you'll have to slow down enough to take it.

What works against it is that your way of coping is to zoom out and move on, and the card asks whether that's fair to the feeling, and to the people attached to it. You can call leaving freedom when it's really avoidance, and look after your own need for space while forgetting the person who needed you to stay. Optimism is lovely. It can also be a very good way of never looking at the hard thing, and I've watched Sagittarius Moons stay cheerful straight through something that needed a cry.

You'll feel it with a partner who notices you drift the moment things get serious, and with family you love warmly from a comfortable distance. In the body it's restlessness, the urge to physically go when feelings press in. When that urge comes, stay put long enough to see what you'd be leaving, and let the heavy feeling be as real to you as the road out.
moon.reversed:
Off true, a Sagittarius Moon runs from every feeling it thinks it can outpace. You keep things light, keep moving, keep the future bright, and any hurt that needs sitting with gets left at the last address. The optimism turns into a way of never facing what's owed, to you or by you.

It shows in the pattern of leaving just before things get real, in friendships kept warm and shallow, in a cheerfulness that won't let anyone, you included, say what's actually wrong. Money can go the same way, spent on getting away. Restlessness spikes whenever a feeling asks you to stay. Pick one heavy thing you've been outrunning and sit with it in one place until you've really looked at it, and let someone see you not be fine.

rising.upright:
Sagittarius rising meets the world wide open. You come across as enthusiastic, direct, up for whatever's over the next hill, and people find you refreshing and a bit unfiltered. Jupiter rules your chart. Justice lends a hand from its sextile, airy to your fire, and adds a measured fairness to all that openness without dampening the enthusiasm. You'll have to choose to use it, though, because your instinct is to blurt the honest thing and keep moving.

The rub is that your directness reads as honesty, which people like, but honesty delivered without much thought can be unfair to whoever's on the receiving end. You'll tell a new person exactly what you think and mean it kindly, and it lands as a judgement they didn't ask for. I've seen Sagittarius risings miss out on a job this way, with the panel liking them enormously and not quite trusting them in front of a client. Justice wants the open manner to take a breath before it speaks.

In a first meeting your candour charms most people and stings the odd one, and a stranger whose beliefs clash with yours brings out the same thing. It shows when you're travelling and forming quick views about a place and the people in it. Walk into the next new room as open as ever, but find out a bit about the person in front of you before you give them your take.
rising.reversed:
Sagittarius rising reversed turns the open, honest front into a careless one. You hand out your verdict on people and places, call it just being straight, and never stop to ask whether the person could take it, so the frankness comes across as tactless or superior. Or the restlessness makes you breezy and non-committal, gone before anyone can hold you to anything.

The candour turns up in a first impression that's a little too pleased with itself, in a stranger left smarting from a truth you tossed off, in preaching a fairness you don't always practise. It can show online too, the confident comment on a stranger's post. Jupiter rules your chart and it likes to hold forth. Ask one new person what they think before you tell them what you think, and stay long enough to be fair to what they say.

sun.upright:
Capricorn Suns play the long game. Cardinal earth, ruled by Saturn, you build things that last, you take responsibility seriously, and you judge a year by what got built in it. Justice stands square to that, three signs off. You're both cardinal and both inclined to push, and the card's Air grinds against your Earth, principle against results, the fair thing against the effective thing. There's an old kinship underneath, though. Saturn is the planet of consequence, and part of you already believes that every action comes with a bill.

The friction is that your instinct is to judge by outcome and rank, and Justice keeps asking whether the way you got the result was fair, and whether the people below you on the ladder were dealt with squarely. You can be scrupulously responsible and still quietly ruthless. The Devil is Capricorn's Major, and it's a card about what ambition can chain you to. Justice asks you to look at the climb as well as the view from the top.

At work it turns up when you deliver and flatten someone in the delivering, and at home in the way you carry everyone and privately keep a record of what it cost. There's a plainer test, too, in how you treat people who can't do anything for you, the junior in their first week, the person on the front desk. Treat them exactly as squarely as the one who signs off on your bonus, and notice how often you already do.
sun.reversed:
A Capricorn Sun reversed lets the ends justify the means and files it under being realistic. The result is all that counts, so a corner cut here, a person used there, a rule bent for the climb, and you tell yourself that's how things get done. Saturn's sense of consequence gets postponed, though with Saturn it always turns up in the end.

It comes out in ambition that treats people as rungs, in coldness toward anyone who can't advance you, in a hard view of other people's failures and a soft one of your own. Sometimes it's the reverse, a fear of failing so strong that you never go for the thing you want. Look at one recent win and ask honestly who paid for it, and put that right before you build the next thing on top of it.

moon.upright:
A Capricorn Moon feels safest in control. You settle yourself by being capable and getting things done, and you'll carry a load alone for a long time before admitting you need a hand. Saturn rules Capricorn, and a Saturn Moon often learned early that someone had to be the grown-up. Justice sits square to that, a hard cardinal angle, its Air pressing on your reserved Earth. Looking at a feeling openly is awkward for you, because feelings are the part you keep managed and out of sight, and duty tends to win.

The friction is that you judge yourself by whether you coped, and the card asks whether that's a fair standard, and whether you're as stern with other people's softness as you are with your own. Coping and being alright are different things. You can do the first for a very long time while the second quietly goes missing, and people around you won't notice, because you look fine. Honestly, you're usually the last to notice too.

With family you're the responsible one who never gets looked after, and in a relationship you give easily and struggle to receive. The body keeps the tally in the jaw and shoulders, sometimes the knees. When you catch yourself soldiering on, ask whether you'd demand the same of someone you love, and let yourself need something out loud, even something small.
moon.reversed:
A Capricorn Moon reversed buries every feeling under work and calls the numbness strength. You cope, you carry, you get on with it, and what you actually need never gets asked, because needing feels like failing. Saturn's weight settles into a grim self-sufficiency that lets no one close enough to help.

You'll find it in the exhaustion you won't admit to, in a hardness toward anyone who seems weak because their softness threatens yours, in duty crowding out every tender thing. It shows with a parent you've always been responsible for. The body sends the bill as a worn-down tiredness and a cold that won't shift. Name one thing you need to one person, and let them give it to you without paying them back straight away.

rising.upright:
People take Capricorn rising seriously from the first handshake. Saturn rules your chart, and you come across as composed, capable and a bit reserved, often older than your years when you're young. Justice stands square to your Ascendant, both cardinal and neither inclined to back down, and its open Air rubs against your careful Earth. With Capricorn rising, Libra is the sign on your tenth house, the top of the chart, so this card sits right on your career and your public name. What you're known for professionally and whether you're known as fair are, for you, very close to the same question.

Your instinct in a new setting is to work out the structure, who's in charge and whether people measure up. The card asks you to see people fairly before you rank them. Strangers can feel assessed and found wanting before you've said much, and to be fair, sometimes they have been. Saturn cares about consequence, so fairness isn't foreign to you. It's just uncomfortable to lead with, because it means showing your hand.

A first meeting where your seriousness reads as cold appraisal is the classic setting, and so is a newcomer who hasn't earned your respect yet. Watch what you do when a junior makes a mistake in front of a client. Give that person the hearing you'd want in their shoes, and let people feel respected by you before they've proven anything.
rising.reversed:
This card upside down can make Capricorn rising look like a panel of judges. You meet new people by ranking them, deciding fast who counts and who doesn't, and strangers feel sized up and dismissed. Or the reserve hardens into a status-conscious chill that keeps everyone at arm's length until they've earned a place you rarely hand out.

It plays out in a first impression that comes across as judging and unreachable, in warming to useful people and freezing out the rest, in respect that only flows upward. With Libra on your tenth, it can also show as a professional reputation for being hard and a bit unfair. Saturn rules your chart and makes you rigid when you're nervous. Give one new person an even hearing regardless of what they can do for you, and notice the warmth you've been holding back as a test.

sun.upright:
Aquarius Suns will stand on a principle when it costs them. Fixed air, ruled by Saturn in the old system and Uranus in the modern one, you think in systems, you care about fairness for everyone, and you're often a step ahead of the argument. Justice meets you in easy agreement, four signs off in the same element, a trine, so this is one of the most natural fits the card has. Reason, impartiality, a level hearing for all, that's already your home ground.

Air on Air means the gift is strong and so is the overshoot. Your fairness can be so wide, fairness for the group, the principle, people in general, that the actual person in front of you gets handled like a case. You'll be scrupulously fair in general and a little distant up close. The Star is Aquarius's Major, a card of hope for everyone, and Justice asks that hope to come down to ground level and land on one particular person. Being fixed, once you've reached a position you're very hard to move, and people who disagree with you may have stopped bothering to say so.

At work you'll fight for the fair system and forget the colleague who just needed you to notice they were having a bad week. Friendships built around shared ideals can end up putting warmth second. The real test is someone whose need is emotional and not at all logical, and whether you can meet it without trying to solve it. Give one person your full, particular attention, the way you'd give it to a cause.
sun.reversed:
An Aquarius Sun reversed hides behind principle and calls the coldness fairness. You judge everything from a height, hand down impartial rulings, and stay detached enough that the person on the other end never feels met, only assessed. The big ideal becomes a way of avoiding the messy, warm, particular business of actual people.

It turns up in a fairness that's generous to humanity and stingy to the friend in the room, and in stubborn positions defended as principle when they're really just yours. It shows in a group project where your rules are right and nobody wants to work with you. Saturn is your traditional ruler, and with this card upside down it makes the stance rigid. Come down from the system to one real person, sit with them up close, and let being fair include being kind.

moon.upright:
An Aquarius Moon handles feelings by stepping back from them. You need space and independence, you connect best through ideas, and you get uneasy when emotion runs too hot or too close. Justice sits a comfortable trine away in the same element, so being fair about a feeling is second nature to you, maybe too much so. When something upsets you, your first move is already to be reasonable about it, to see it from every angle and not make a fuss.

Air on Air is where the catch is. You can be so fair and so detached about your own feelings that you never let yourself have them. You'll grant everyone their side, understand the person who hurt you, stay admirably level, and the raw feeling gets filed away without being felt. Saturn, your traditional ruler, likes things kept orderly, and feelings are messy. I've known Aquarius Moons explain a breakup calmly and kindly to everyone they know and only fall apart about it two years later.

A partner may feel you're kind but somewhere else, and the friend you help gets clear, sensible advice from a slight distance. In the body it can be a numb, in-your-head feeling when things run high. Let one feeling be unreasonable and yours for a while, and ask yourself whether all that fairness is costing you the closeness you quietly want.
moon.reversed:
An Aquarius Moon reversed uses reason to float above every feeling it doesn't want. You stay so level, so understanding, so far above the fray that nothing actually touches you, and the people close to you feel loved in theory and lonely in practice. It keeps you safe, and it also means nobody can quite get to you when you need them.

You'll see it in a relationship where you're never the one who cracks, in friendships kept warm at a careful distance, in turning a hurt into an idea until there's nothing left to feel. Being fixed, the coolness sets hard, and it can go on for years. Uranus, your modern ruler, tends to break away at exactly the point where it would have to stay and feel something. Let someone see one feeling before you've made it reasonable, and let them respond to it.

rising.upright:
Aquarius rising treats the stranger and the chief executive exactly the same. You come across as friendly, original, a little cool, and people notice quite quickly that you don't play favourites. Saturn rules your chart traditionally, Uranus in modern terms. Justice flows straight into that manner, a trine in the same element, so the even, impartial quality is doubled, and it's genuinely one of your strengths that everyone gets the same level hearing from you whatever their rank.

The overshoot is that your even-handedness can be so cool it reads as not quite caring. Each person gets treated as an equal, which is lovely, and nobody gets treated as special. A new person can feel accurately judged by you without feeling seen at all. Justice at its best is fair and warm. Yours can be fair and slightly remote, and some people will need the warmth before they'll trust the fairness.

It shows in meeting new people, where you're likeable and hard to get close to, and especially with anyone who wanted a more personal response than your even manner gives. It shows at work in feedback that's scrupulously balanced and a bit bloodless. Keep the fairness, people rely on it. Let one stranger feel individually noticed by you as well, and remember something small about them for next time.
rising.reversed:
Aquarius rising reversed turns the even manner cold and contrary. You treat everyone the same to the point of treating no one warmly, or you meet new people with a reflexive detachment that keeps them at a principled arm's length. The fairness is there and nobody can feel it.

It comes across in a first impression where you seem above it all, in arguing the contrarian side on principle and losing the actual person, in a friendliness that never quite lets anyone in. It shows in groups, where you're respected and rarely asked along for drinks afterwards. Uranus, your modern ruler, likes to be different, and here it's keeping everyone out. Meet the next new person as a particular individual, ask them something personal, and let a little warmth come through.

sun.upright:
Pisces Suns feel with everyone. Mutable water, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, you forgive easily, the line between you and other people is thin, and you'd sooner flow round a hard edge than stand on it. Justice comes in at a strange angle. Pisces and Libra sit five signs apart, a quincunx, which means the two have almost nothing in common and keep having to make small adjustments to sit together at all. Air and Water are neutral elements, so there's no help from that side either. The card is clear and boundaried and holds a sword, and what it holds out to you is the thing you find hardest, a straight line.

Your compassion doesn't like to judge. Handing down a hard verdict feels unkind, and the card keeps insisting that fairness sometimes means saying this is yours and this is mine, this far and no further. That's a fairness to yourself as much as to anyone else, and Pisces Suns are often the last people they're fair to. The Moon is your sign's Major, a card of blurred edges and half-light. Justice is its opposite in mood, everything sharp, and you're being asked to borrow a little of that.

With a partner you give until there's nothing left and call it love, and in a friendship the boundary can blur so far that you've taken on someone else's whole life. Money is often what you can't say no about, the loan, the bill you cover. Draw one clear line where you'd usually give way, and keep to it for a month.
sun.reversed:
A Pisces Sun reversed lets every boundary dissolve and calls the formlessness compassion. You forgive what shouldn't be waved through, take on blame that isn't yours, give past the point of being fair to yourself, and the scales never come out because judging anything feels cold. Somebody ends up treated unfairly, and the person who loses out is usually you.

It shows in relationships where you lose yourself entirely, in saying yes when everything in you means no, in a martyrdom that quietly resents the people it serves. When it all gets too much, escape can follow, too much sleep, too much wine, too many hours on the phone. Jupiter rules Pisces and gives without counting. Count once. Name what's fair to you as well as to them, and draw one clean line.

moon.upright:
A Pisces Moon soaks up whatever's in the room. Other people's moods become your weather, you need quiet and retreat and dreaming to recover, and you often can't tell where your feelings end and someone else's begin. Justice arrives from an awkward five-sign angle, clear Air meeting boundless Water with nothing in common between them. Putting a feeling up to be judged fairly takes constant small adjustment, because your instinct is to merge with a feeling. Judging it at all means drawing a line, and lines are what you dissolve.

The tension is that you take on emotions that were never yours to carry and call it empathy, and the card asks whose feeling this actually is before you go under. Not every hurt in the room belongs to you. Some of it belongs to the person it happened to, and they may need to feel it themselves. Jupiter rules your Moon, and Jupiter enlarges, so you can end up feeling other people's pain bigger than they do.

Anyone in pain near you can flood you until you can barely function, and in a close relationship you can feel everything they feel and lose track of your own outline. In the body it lands as being swamped, needing to get under the doona and sleep. When you're overwhelmed, sort the feelings into yours and not yours, and hand the second pile back, kindly.
moon.reversed:
A Pisces Moon reversed goes under and loses the scales entirely. You absorb everyone's pain, can't tell it from your own, forgive what hurt you before you've looked at it, and drift into fog or fantasy when the flood gets too high. The fair measure the card asks for needs a boundary, and a boundary is the last thing you want to draw.

You'll feel it getting swept into other people's crises as if they were yours, in a compassion with no floor that leaves you empty, in escaping when you could be facing what's fair to you. The body pays with exhaustion and a washed-out heaviness, and sleep stops restoring you. Neptune, your modern ruler, blurs things. Pick one feeling and decide plainly whether it's yours or someone else's, and act on the answer.

rising.upright:
Pisces rising meets the world softly. You're receptive and a little dreamy, you mirror whoever's in front of you so well that you almost become them, and strangers find you hard to pin down and easy to confide in. Jupiter rules your chart, with Neptune as the modern ruler. Justice comes at you from a quincunx, five signs off, its clear, discerning Air a foreign thing to your soft Water, so a clear-eyed read of a stranger takes real, deliberate adjustment. Your instinct is to merge with people. The card wants you to look at them.

The tension is that your open manner takes everyone in without much discernment, and Justice wants you to keep a line, to notice who's being straight with you before you dissolve into them. You can be so receptive that you have no read at all on whether a new person is trustworthy until you're already involved. Pisces risings get told a stranger's life story on the train. That's a gift. It also means the charming ones get in very easily.

Meeting someone new, you tend to absorb their mood and lose your own footing, and a smooth talker can take you in before you've noticed what they're after. It shows on first dates and in new jobs, especially with a boss who's very warm very fast. Stay as soft as ever with the next new person, but hold back one thing about yourself until they've shown you who they are.
rising.reversed:
Pisces rising reversed loses itself in whoever it meets. You mirror so completely that there's no edge of your own left, take in every stranger without any real assessment, and end up shaped by the last strong person in the room. The clear reading the card offers dissolves before it can form.

The pattern shows early, when a new person can turn you into whatever they need, and in being charmed or used by someone you never stopped to size up. It shows in a vagueness that lets other people define you. Neptune, your modern ruler, loves a blur, and first impressions are where it does the most harm. Meet one new person while staying clearly yourself, notice whether they're straight with you, and say no to one small thing they ask.

1.upright:
Justice in the first house puts the card of the seventh house in the first, which is a bit like finding your partner's coat on your own hook. The first is you, your body, the way you carry yourself, how you start things. It's naturally Aries's house and Mars's, quick and self-directed, and Libra sits exactly opposite. So the card comes into the house of 'me' carrying the concerns of 'us', and it asks who you are when you're being fair. Air and Fire get along, so this tends to sharpen you. It's an angular house too, one of the chart's four corners, which means whatever the card is doing here, people will see it.

What's live is a pull to define yourself by fairness, to lead with an even hand. That can be a real strength, a self that starts from principle and is known for it. It can also mean you find it hard to locate yourself without someone across the table to measure against, so your sense of who you are waits on other people's verdict. Mercury has its joy in this house, and you may find you think more clearly about yourself when you talk it through out loud with someone.

It shows in how you present and how you begin things, whether you walk into a new job or a new friendship as a fair dealer or as someone still hoping to be judged fair.
