It shows in the body as a more upright, considered way of carrying yourself. Work out one thing you stand for that doesn't depend on anyone agreeing with you, and lead with it.
1.reversed:
Upside down in the first house, Justice can leave your sense of self hanging on other people's approval. You get so shaped by whether others see you as fair that there's no one underneath the reflection, and you keep adjusting yourself to the room. Or the even, reasonable front covers someone who isn't being straight, with others or with themselves.

It touches how you begin things and how you're read, coming across as balanced while feeling hollow behind it, or picking fights just to feel like a definite person. Mars rules this house naturally and doesn't like being second-guessed, so the swing between people-pleasing and sudden stubbornness can be sharp. The body can carry the strain of holding a pose. Find one thing about yourself that stands whether or not anyone approves, and start from there.

2.upright:
Money is what the second house is about, the actual money, what comes in, what goes out, what you own, and underneath all that, what you think you're worth. It's Taurus's house and Venus rules it, and Venus also rules Libra, so Justice lands here with a family connection. That's where the ease ends. Libra and Taurus sit five signs apart, a quincunx, and Air and Earth are opposed elements, so the idea of fair worth runs straight into the hard figure on the statement. The two need a lot of small adjustments to agree.

What's live is whether what you have was fairly earned and is fairly held. Justice in this house wants your earnings clean and your dealings square, nothing owed where nobody can see it and nothing taken that wasn't yours. It weighs self-worth too, and with this card that very often means someone who's been undercharging for years. The second house is succedent, the part of the chart where things are built up and kept, so the card is looking at the money habits you've held onto a long time.

It shows in pay and pricing, whether you ask for a fair rate or talk yourself down before anyone else can. It shows in any money split where fairness is on the line, an inheritance, a shared account, a loan between friends. Write down what you'd charge a stranger for your work, compare it with what you actually charge, and close the gap.
2.reversed:
A crooked ledger is how Justice reversed tends to show in the second house. What you take and what you give stop matching, and Venus keeps trying to smooth it over so you don't have to look. It might be underpaying yourself, quietly overspending, or hanging onto money that fairly belongs to someone else. On the surface the account looks fine.

It reaches into pay you resent and won't renegotiate, a shared cost carried unevenly, a debt on either side that nobody mentions. Self-worth can run crooked too, valuing yourself well under the honest mark, or well over it to cover the fear. It often goes back to how money was talked about, or never talked about, in the house you grew up in. Put the real figures on one page and read them, and fix the one account you've been avoiding.

3.upright:
The third house is the everyday voice. Your words, your messages, the way you learn and explain things, your brothers and sisters, your neighbours, the short trips that make up an ordinary week. It's naturally Gemini's house, ruled by Mercury, an air house, and Justice is air too, four signs along in a trine. Fairness slips straight into how you talk and think here. It's a genuinely happy placement, a mind that hears both sides and a voice that gets to the point.

Air doubling Air does bring the usual risk of too much. At its best your speech is fair, clear and trusted, and people come to you to settle a disagreement because you'll give each side a proper hearing. Overdone, you can argue any side so well that cleverness starts standing in for truth, or keep a point open forever without landing on the plain answer. The Moon has its joy in this house, a reminder that the way things are said matters as much as what's said, especially in a family.

It shows in conversations and texts and how you handle a disagreement in words, and with a sibling where there's an old question about who said what, or who got more. It touches how you learn, checking sources before you believe them. Reach for the plain thing over the clever one, and let the other person finish before you reply.
3.reversed:
The fair voice turns one-sided when Justice is reversed in the third house. Your words start pressing a conclusion you reached before the other person spoke, and all that airy skill goes into winning the exchange. You can make a crooked case sound perfectly reasonable, and doubled Air makes the spin very fluent.

It lives in arguments where you score points and lose the truth, in emails worded to protect you more than to be straight, in a sibling or neighbour dispute where one voice drowns out the other. Learning tilts too, taking in only what agrees with you. Mercury rules this house and loves being quick. Slow the talk down, repeat back what the other person said before you answer it, and say the plain version even when a sharper line is right there.

4.upright:
Home and roots belong to the fourth house, the family you came from, the private ground nobody outside sees, the home you make yourself. Justice sits square to this house's natural sign, Libra three signs off from Cancer and sharing only the cardinal push, and its cool Air doesn't blend easily with the deep Water of family. The two have to be introduced. In practice that means fairness and family feeling don't automatically agree, and this placement makes you work out where they meet. It's an angular house, so whatever comes up here won't stay quiet.

What's live is whether the accounts at home are square. Who does the emotional work, who gets thanked and who doesn't, who was owed something years ago and never got it, what one person carried for everyone. Justice in the fourth often inherits an old family imbalance and wants it looked at properly before it gets handed down again. The Moon rules this house, and family memory is long, so it's worth being careful about whose version you're working from.

It shows in the household split of chores and money, in a long-running family unfairness that you seem to be the only one who notices, and in how you make your own home a place where things are even. It can show around an ageing parent and who's doing the caring. Name the imbalance at home that everyone tiptoes around, calmly, at a time when nobody's already upset.
4.reversed:
When Justice turns over in the fourth house, home is standing on a tilted floor. An old family unfairness never got looked at, a truth stayed unspoken, a load fell on one person for years, and the whole private ground leans because of it. Home doesn't settle while that stays crooked underneath.

It shows in the family role you got handed and never agreed to, in an unspoken debt between you and a parent or sibling, in recreating an uneven home because it's the only kind you ever learned. The square to Cancer makes it prickly, and the Moon keeps it emotional, so it tends to come out at family gatherings and big dinners. The body can hold it as never quite relaxing at home. Bring the imbalance up with the people it involves, and stop paying a debt that was never fairly yours.

5.upright:
The fifth house is where you play. Romance, creativity, children, hobbies, whatever you'd do on a free afternoon because you love it. It's naturally Leo's house, ruled by the Sun, and Justice comes in on friendly terms, a sextile, Air feeding Fire. There's a lovely detail in the old scheme too. Venus has her joy in the fifth house, and Venus rules Libra, the sign this card belongs to, so the planet behind Justice is especially happy here. What that gives you is a sense that pleasure and romance are best when they're even, when nobody's keeping a secret tally.

What's live is the fairness of your fun. Whether love and creativity here are a real exchange, or a show where one person supplies the delight and the other enjoys it. Being a sextile, the fair version is on offer and you'll have to choose it, because play tends to run on impulse. The fifth is also where children sit in the chart, and fairness between siblings, who got the bigger slice, who got the later bedtime, is exactly the kind of thing this card notices.

It shows in a romance and whether it's balanced or lopsided, in a creative collaboration and whose name ends up on it, and in what you say when a child cries 'that's not fair'. Look at who plans the dates, who starts the fun, who does the making, and if it's always the same person, change it.
5.reversed:
The delight runs lopsided when Justice is reversed in the fifth. One person carries the romance or the fun while the other coasts, credit for a creative thing lands with the wrong name, or you put on an ease you don't feel to keep the good time going. After a while the fun goes out of it for both of you.

It shows in a romance where you give far more of the warmth than you get, in a creative partnership where your part goes unmentioned, in play that's turned into a performance. With children, favouritism, even the unintended kind, can quietly set a pattern. The Sun rules this house and wants to shine, and Venus wants things lovely, and together they can paper over a lot. Rebalance the give-and-take honestly, and let yourself be on the receiving end for once.

6.upright:
The sixth house is the daily grind of keeping yourself going. The routine, the job you actually do each day, the small habits that keep the body running, what you eat, when you sleep, whether you move. It's naturally Virgo's house, Mercury's, and Justice sits right next door, near but speaking a different language, its Air against the Earth of the body. The fair idea and the physical fact need patient adjusting to line up. This is the house where cause and effect are easiest to see, because what you do shows up in how you feel within a few days.

What's live is balance in the plainest sense. Work and rest kept fair to each other. What you put into the body set against what it actually needs. Justice in the sixth reads the body as an honest record, steady, even habits returning steady energy and neglect turning up later as a bill. Mars has its joy here, and it's the planet that likes to push, so there's a real risk of treating the body as something to be driven harder.

It shows in your working day and whether the load is fair, in sleep and food and exercise and whether you treat yourself squarely, and in a workplace where one person does the jobs nobody else wants. Pick the one habit that's gone furthest out of balance, work or rest or food, and even it out over a few weeks, without punishing yourself for it.
6.reversed:
Justice upside down in the sixth house lets the daily balance tip and looks the other way. A habit pushed too far starts coming due in the body, and instead of looking at your everyday choices you blame circumstances or push harder. The body keeps an honest count even when you won't.

It shows in a routine skewed toward work and starved of rest, or the reverse, in a health matter you've been putting off, in a job where an unfair daily load is grinding you down and you haven't said so. Mars has its joy in this house and can turn upkeep into a punishment. Mercury rules it and can turn it into worry. Take plain, kind responsibility for the habit that's out of balance, and bring the daily give-and-take back toward level.

7.upright:
This is the card's home ground. The seventh house is naturally Libra's, Venus rules it, and Justice is Libra's own Major, so the card lands here with nothing to translate. Air in an air house. The seventh is the person across from you, a partner, a business partner, anyone you've signed something with, even an open opponent, and when a card lands in the house of its own sign it speaks at full volume. The whole subject here is fairness between two people. It's an angular house, so it won't be subtle.

What's live is the plainest question the card asks anywhere, whether this partnership is even. Whether both people carry a true share, of the money, the housework, the planning, the worry, the apologies. With a placement this pure there's very little cover. I'd say most partnerships, even good ones, turn out to be carrying some quiet imbalance when you really look, and this card tends to make you look.

It shows in a marriage or long relationship and how the weight is split, in a contract or agreement and whether its terms are square, and in how you deal with someone who is openly against you, a landlord, an ex, the other side of a negotiation. Sit down with your partner, or on your own if need be, and list who does what over an ordinary fortnight. Then talk about the list itself and leave blame out of it.
7.reversed:
Tipped scales between two people is what this card shows reversed in the seventh. One person over-gives while the other coasts, or a truth stays unsaid across the table, and because this is the card's own house the imbalance is stark and hard to dress up. A partnership can't sit level while one side carries most of it.

It shows in a relationship where you've slowly taken on the bigger share, in a contract whose terms quietly favour one party, in blaming the person opposite for a gap you both made. It can show in a business partnership too, where one person does the work and the other takes the meetings. Venus rules this house, and Venus hates raising an uncomfortable number and will keep things pleasant for as long as it can. Say what's actually owed between you, in plain figures or plain words, before you decide what the partnership is.

8.upright:
The eighth house is shared territory, and deep. Sex and intimacy, other people's money mixed with yours, debts, loans, inheritances, tax, and the big endings that change you. It's naturally Scorpio's house, ruled by Mars and in modern astrology Pluto, and Justice comes in from right next door, a neighbour that speaks a different language. Its clear Air is a stranger to the deep Water here, so bringing fairness into places that are usually kept private takes a deliberate reach. The eighth likes things in the dark. The card wants them where everyone can see.

What's live is a fair reckoning where accounts are normally hidden. Honesty in intimacy, an even hand in what you and another person hold in common, a debt or a will looked at openly. Justice in the eighth says that even a hard ending goes more cleanly when the accounts are square. It's a good card here for anyone sorting out a joint account after a separation, or talking honestly with a partner about intimacy and what each of you needs from it.

It shows in shared finances and whether they're fairly kept, in the give-and-take of physical and emotional closeness, and in an inheritance or a debt where old family feelings come up. Have the money conversation you've both been avoiding, with the actual figures on the table.
8.reversed:
A crooked account hidden in the dark is the reversed Justice in the eighth house. A shared debt, an inheritance, an intimacy where the give-and-take was never fair and never discussed. Because this house keeps its secrets, the imbalance can sit unseen for a long time, bending everything built on top of it. What's shared stops being fair and nobody says so.

It shows in joint money handled unevenly and in silence, in intimacy where one person holds most of the power, in a will or a debt that quietly short-changed someone. Sometimes it's a secret about money kept from a partner. Endings drag and won't finish while the account stays tilted. Mars rules this house, and here it fights in private. Bring the buried imbalance up where both people can see it, and let the hard thing end once it's square.

9.upright:
Belief, study and distance are the ninth house's territory. What you think life is for, what you study, the long trips, the foreign places, the teachers and the books that change your mind. It's naturally Sagittarius's house and Jupiter's, and Justice reaches it on friendly terms, a sextile, Air feeding Fire. Fairness and the big picture cooperate here, if you choose to let them. The Sun has its joy in the ninth, so this is a house where things want to be seen clearly, in full light.

What's live is whether your beliefs are fair. Whether the convictions you've reasoned or travelled your way toward hold up when you test them squarely, including against people who see it differently. Justice in the ninth is very good at catching the belief that judges everyone by a rule it lets itself off, and it asks your worldview to be as fair as you'd want anyone else's to be. That can be uncomfortable for people who've held the same opinions since school.

It shows in what you hold true and whether you've tested it or just inherited it, in study and whether you give the other side's best argument a proper read, and in travel that puts you among people who live differently. It can show around official paperwork too, a visa, a course application, anything a formal body decides. Read one serious argument against something you believe, all the way through, and see what survives.
9.reversed:
In the ninth house, reversed, a belief hardens into a double standard. A conviction you hold judges others by a rule you quietly excuse yourself from, and the fair look the card asks for gets skipped because you've decided you already know. The worldview stops being examined and starts being defended.

It shows in a faith or philosophy worn like armour, in study that only takes in what agrees with you, in preaching a fairness abroad that you don't practise at home. Jupiter rules this house and it makes certainty feel generous, which is exactly how it slips past you. It can show in a falling-out with a teacher or a mentor. Pick one long-settled conviction and reopen it honestly, preferably with someone who disagrees with you and who you respect.

10.upright:
The tenth house is the top of the chart. Your career, your public role, your reputation, what people who don't know you personally would say you do. It's naturally Capricorn's house and Saturn's, and Justice lands square to it, both cardinal and both pushing, with the card's Air grinding against the Earth of the career house. There's a real friction here between what's fair and what gets you ahead, and this placement makes your name and your integrity the same question. It's angular and it's public, so how you handle that question will be seen.

What's live is whether your standing was fairly earned, and whether credit lands where it belongs, on you and on the people who helped. Justice in the tenth builds a reputation on straight dealing, the kind of professional name people trust because your decisions hold up when examined. It also notices when credit or blame falls in the wrong place, and it minds. Saturn rules this house and it's the planet of consequence, so what you do here tends to follow you for years, in both directions.

It shows in your career and whether you got where you are cleanly, in a promotion or a public thank-you and who really earned it, and in how you use whatever authority you have over other people. It shows in a performance review, on either side of the desk. Make sure the credit and the blame land where they honestly belong, including on you when it's genuinely yours.
10.reversed:
Justice reversed at the top of the chart tilts the public reckoning. Credit lands on the wrong name or blame falls on the wrong person, or a reputation rests on something that wouldn't survive a straight look. The name holds up in public while the record behind it runs crooked.

It shows in taking credit that wasn't fully yours, in a career move made by cutting a corner you don't mention, in being blamed publicly for something that wasn't your doing. It can show with a boss who plays favourites, and in your own temptation to do the same. Saturn rules the tenth, and with Saturn things left alone tend to set hard. Set the professional record straight while it can still be changed, and make sure the credit sits with whoever actually earned it, yourself included.

11.upright:
The eleventh house is your people in the plural. Friends, networks, clubs, the group chat, the causes you give time to, and the hopes you pin on the future. It's naturally Aquarius's house, ruled by Saturn and in modern astrology Uranus, and Justice flows in easily, a trine, Air meeting Air. Jupiter has its joy here as well, so there's a generous, open kind of fairness on offer among your friends and groups. This placement wants those circles to run on real give-and-take.

Because it's Air amplifying Air, the fair instinct is strong and can drift into the abstract. At its best you're the one who keeps a group honest, who notices when someone's carrying more than their share of a shared plan and says so kindly. Overdone, your fairness gets so high-minded and collective that the particular friend in front of you feels like a policy. I've seen this a lot with people who run things, committees, sporting clubs, community groups.

It shows in a friendship and whether it's an even exchange, in a group or network where the work and the credit should be shared, and in a shared cause where not everyone is pulling equally. It shows in who always organises the catch-up and who always turns up late to it. Look at your closest three friendships and ask who reaches out first, and if it's always you or never you, do something about it.
11.reversed:
A circle goes out of true when Justice is reversed in the eleventh house. One friend carries the group, a shared hope rests on an uneven deal, or the fairness you talk about for everyone never quite reaches the person beside you. The imbalance spreads quietly and can split people before anyone names it.

It shows in a friendship where you always give or always take, in a group project where the work falls unequally, in high ideals about fairness that somehow skip your actual friends. Sometimes it's a friendship that's drifted because nobody wanted to raise it. Doubled Air keeps it abstract and cool, and Saturn, the traditional ruler here, can make a group rigid about its own rules. Look at what's fair among your people plainly, friend by friend, and fix the one where somebody is carrying the rest.

12.upright:
The twelfth house is the hidden part of the chart. The things you do alone, sleep and dreams, what you retreat into, what works on you without your quite knowing. It's naturally Pisces's house, ruled by Jupiter and in modern astrology Neptune, and Justice arrives at an awkward five-sign angle, clear Air in a watery place where edges blur. Bringing a fair look into the dark takes constant small adjustment. There's a fitting detail underneath, though. Saturn has its joy in the twelfth, and Saturn is the old planet of conscience and consequence, which sits close to what this card cares about.

What's live is a reckoning that happens out of sight. A conscience already working on something your waking mind hasn't named, a buried account quietly asking to be settled. Justice in the twelfth often means the fairest part of you works in the background, in dreams, in solitude, in the nagging sense that something isn't square long before you can say what. Look at the veil hanging between the two pillars behind the figure. Nobody in the picture can see past it, and that's roughly how this placement feels from the inside.

It shows in what you carry without seeing it, an old guilt or an old grievance you steer by, and in the need for time alone to hear yourself think.
